stimuli.description: Descriptions of 18 common rooms or spaces in a home (e.g., entryway, kitchen, living room, garage, backyard) and a list of 29 ambiance options (e.g., organization, privacy, productivity, rejuvenation, romance, safety, tranquility, wealth).

tables.description: List of the 29 ambiance options used in the Inventory of Desired Ambiances in the Ideal Home (IDAIH).
Data on which Figure 1 (blueprint plan depicting top five ambiances desired in each room) is based.

limitations: Survey-based findings about ideal spaces need to be followed up with studies of what people really do to their own spaces or whether their responses instead reflect naive theories about themselves and others.
Questions are raised about the extent to which ambiances are directed to the occupants themselves versus visitors.
The current data do not permit analyses of which variables determine whether a person would prefer to evoke a sense of, say, abundance rather than togetherness in their kitchen.
The study did not examine how ambiances are affected by factors such as income, gender, culture, age, class, ownership status (owned/rented), or living arrangements (alone/with others).
